name: Face Skin Smoothness
description: Analyzes excessive skin smoothness from AI generation
algorithm: Face Skin Smoothness — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes facial skin smoothness for video deepfake detection:

1. **Skin Region Segmentation**: Facial skin regions are segmented per frame, separating skin from eyes, eyebrows, lips, and hair. The skin regions — forehead, cheeks, nose, chin — are analyzed independently for texture quality.

2. **Texture Frequency Analysis**: High-frequency skin texture content is measured using local power spectral density. Natural skin contains multi-scale texture: pores (~0.5-1mm spacing), fine wrinkles, and skin grain. The method quantifies texture energy at these characteristic spatial frequencies. AI-generated skin often shows suppressed high-frequency texture — the over-smoothing artifact common in GAN-generated faces.

3. **Smoothness Gradient Detection**: The method maps smoothness variation across the face. Natural faces show region-dependent smoothness: smoother on cheeks, more textured on the nose and forehead. Deepfake faces may show unnaturally uniform smoothness or incorrect smoothness distribution across facial regions.

4. **Skin Detail Preservation Assessment**: Fine skin details (individual pores, hair follicles, micro-wrinkles) are evaluated for rendering quality. These details help assess whether the skin texture is photographed (with characteristic sensor-captured detail) versus rendered (often lacking sub-pixel detail or showing repetitive synthetic patterns).

5. **Temporal Skin Texture Stability**: Natural skin texture is static — pores and micro-features remain in fixed positions frame-to-frame. The method tracks skin texture consistency over time. Deepfake generators may produce temporally varying skin texture where pore patterns shift, appear, or disappear between frames, creating detectable temporal texture instability.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through face skin smoothness analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
